keyFormulas.tex: w^\star = \frac{\sum_i (x_i-\bar x)(y_i-\bar y)}{\sum_i (x_i-\bar x)^2},\quad b^\star = \bar y - w^\star \bar x

nodes.title: Support Vector Machines
nodes.summary: Among all separating lines, choose the one with the widest margin. Only the support vectors matter.
objectives: Define the geometric margin 2/‖w‖
Identify support vectors from the dual variables α

keyFormulas.label: Soft-margin primal
keyFormulas.tex: \min_{\mathbf w,b}\ \tfrac12\|\mathbf w\|^2 + C\sum_i \max\big(0,\,1 - y_i(\mathbf w^\top\mathbf x_i + b)\big)

keyFormulas.label: Dual
keyFormulas.tex: \max_{\alpha}\ \sum_i \alpha_i - \tfrac12\sum_{i,j}\alpha_i\alpha_j y_i y_j\,\mathbf x_i^\top\mathbf x_j,\quad 0\le\alpha_i\le C,\ \sum_i\alpha_i y_i = 0

challenge.prompt: You delete a training point that lies far outside the margin on the correct side. What happens to the trained SVM?
options: The boundary shifts towards where the point was
Nothing — its dual variable α is zero, so it does not contribute to w
challenge.explanation: Only support vectors (α > 0) appear in w = Σ αᵢyᵢxᵢ. A point strictly outside the margin has α = 0, so removing it leaves the solution unchanged.

challenge.prompt: A linear RNN has a recurrent matrix whose singular values all equal 0.9. Roughly how large is the gradient reaching 50 steps back, relative to the last step?
challenge.explanation: The gradient is multiplied by 0.9 at every step: 0.9⁵⁰ ≈ 0.0052. That is the vanishing-gradient problem.

challenge.prompt: Why are attention scores divided by √d_k?
options: Dot products of random d_k-dimensional vectors have variance ∝ d_k; scaling keeps the softmax from saturating
To normalise each row to sum to one
challenge.explanation: If q and k have unit-variance components, q·k has variance d_k. Large scores push softmax into regions with vanishing gradients; dividing by √d_k restores unit variance.
